A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same R3DM research work. All 21 pages of each version, including figures, equations, tables, and Appendices A–C, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original SMAC and SMACv2 experiments, comparative learning curves, qualitative policy analysis, and ablations in Section 5 and Figures 2–5.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experimental results, qualitative analyses, and ablations.

M1.justification: The operative method remains unchanged: contrastive learning, both intrinsic rewards, the final TD loss, network architectures, and Algorithm 1 are retained. The conditional-MI revisions concern the theoretical justification rather than the specified training procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six SMAC scenarios and six SMACv2 scenarios, with the same qualitative and ablation settings. No evaluated task or environment coverage changes.

E2.justification: Figures 2–3 retain QMIX, ACORM, CIA, GoMARL, CDS, and EMC as comparators. The ACORM qualitative comparison and ablation variants also remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Evaluation metrics, training settings, and testing procedures are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same hyperparameter tables and evaluation every 5,000 updates using 32 episodes.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Figure 4 retain the same policy and role-embedding case study. Section 5.4 and Figure 5 retain the imagination-horizon, role-cardinality, and contrastive-learning ablations.

E5.justification: Both versions report evaluations on the same five random seeds and retain mean curves with standard-deviation shading, explicitly described in Figure 3. Statistical reporting in the ablations is unchanged.

E6.justification: Figures 2–5 are visually identical, retaining the same learning curves, uncertainty bands, qualitative outcomes, and ablation findings. No numerical corrections or additional results were identified.

T1.justification: Equation 2 and Theorems 4.1 and 4.3 replace unconditional MI with MI conditioned on past history. Appendix A.1 revises the marginalization and lower-bound derivation, replacing p(e|history,role) ≈ p(e|role) with sufficiency assumptions and p(e|history) ≈ p(e). Appendix A.3 also revises its MI expansion. These changes alter the central formal objective and theoretical guarantees, rather than merely their notation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: connecting roles to future behavior through dynamics-based intrinsic rewards, integrating with ACORM, and reporting up to 20% win-rate improvement.

C2.justification: Interpretations of coordination, exploration, role specialization, and long-horizon prediction errors are unchanged. Section 6 retains the limitations concerning preset role counts and dynamics models that omit other agents’ actions and roles.

D1.justification: Appendices B–C retain identical implementation details, architectures, hyperparameters, reward formulas, and pseudocode. The stated code access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work discussion are unchanged, including positioning against existing role-based methods and the relationship to ACORM and Dreamer.

P1.justification: Section 4.1 is renamed from 'Role-based Diversity Objective' to 'Role Representation Learning Objective.' Limited explanatory prose is revised around history conditioning and the Appendix A.1 assumptions; the overall narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Revised equations change local typesetting, and the expanded Appendix A.1 redistributes proof blocks across pages 12–15. Figures, tables, captions, and the algorithm display remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V4’s conditional formulation better matches the history-conditioned likelihood ratios in Theorem 4.3. However, revised Appendix A.1 assumes p(e|history) ≈ p(e) despite defining e as a function of history, and inconsistently retains unconditioned probabilities in intermediate steps. These unresolved issues prevent establishing that the central bound is better justified. With the practical method and empirical evidence unchanged, the net quality effect remains uncertain.
